item.title: Chaos Growth in a Generic 2D Hamiltonian System
item.description: arXiv:2611.11255v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine the geometric mechanism controlling the transition from local to global chaos in a generic 2D Hamiltonian system, the generalized H\'{e}non-Heiles system. Using Poincar\'e sections and invariant manifolds, we show that the chaotic fraction grows through abrupt transitions associated with the destruction of invariant barriers. We introduce an index that gives the time required for the first penetration of a local chaotic domain into the global chaos. This index increases sharply and tends to infinity as a critical energy is approached. The set of lobes generates heteroclinic connections, while multiple unstable periodic orbits exhibit a global manifold structure characterised by repeated loops and lobes. However, in special chaotic cases close to the integrable H\'{e}non-Heiles potential, where two asymptotic curves extend to infinity, the manifold topology differs qualitatively from the generic case, as the asymptotic curves no longer form closed structures surrounding the periodic orbits.
item.dc:creator: Athanasios C. Tzemos, George Contopoulos

item.title: A Poisson-bracket operator for Hamiltonian separability: intrinsic geometry and exact defects
item.description: arXiv:2611.12015v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Additive separation of the Hamilton-Jacobi equation depends on the Hamiltonian and on the canonical variables, and this paper introduces a five-input Poisson-bracket operator whose values on canonical pairs reproduce the Levi-Civita separability expressions. On a symplectic product structure its off-diagonal values are intrinsic, since they equal a symplectic pairing of the sector Hamiltonian fields and measure the Frobenius obstruction of a Lagrangian distribution, and their vanishing yields a local separation theorem. Because the operator is cubic in the Hamiltonian, its perturbation expansion is exact and defines a linearised separability operator and a defect functional. For Hamiltonians with a cyclic angle, the linearised operator divided by the squared rotor frequency is an angle derivative of the Melnikov integrand, so that the defect integrated along a homoclinic orbit decides the first-order splitting of the separatrix. Closed-form defects are obtained for the polar-nodal normal forms of satellite theory and, through a covariance of the operator on level sets, for Kerr geodesics. Used for coordinate selection, the defect singles out the separating focal distance of the Euler two-centre problem as its unique nondegenerate minimum, and for axisymmetric potentials it shows that the prescriptions of Sanders and Vasiliev are two weightings of the same St\"ackel residual. The residual selector and Binney's shell-orbit fit improve both actions over the median prescription for 48 and 50 of 50 orbits in a flattened logarithmic potential, whereas the operator selector lowers the 90th-percentile action spread of 50 orbits in a Miyamoto-Nagai potential from 2.90% to 0.91%.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Martinusi

item.title: Validating direct solvers for Newton's gravitational N-body problem, and the systematic comparison between IEEE floating point and Posits
item.description: arXiv:2608.17032v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a systematic comparison between arbitrary precise arithmetic and integration, IEEE-754 compliant floating point arithmetic (fp16, bfp16, fp32, double precision fp64, and quadruple precision fp128), and two implementations of Posits (type III unum) for solving Newton's chaotic N-body problem. Each implementation is benchmarked with arbitrary precise calculations to objectively evaluate their performance in precision as well as speed. We rely on hardware and compiler implementations for fp64, and software implementations for arbitrary-precision arithmetic and Posits. Half precision arithmetic (fp16, bfp16, and Posits$<16,1>$) are insufficiently precise for solving Newton's equations of motion. Single precision (fp32, and Posits$<32,2>$) could be used for statistical ensemble calculations, but lead to relatively large errors in any individual strong encounter. All 64-bit implementations fp64 as well as Posits (Posits$<64,3>$) experience difficulty in our tests. One of the implementations of Posits (Universal) gives precision comparable to fp64 but is slow (by at least an orders of magnitude compared to fp64 after correcting for the more efficient hardware support for the latter). The other (CPPPosits) has a speed comparable to fp64 but has systematically larger errors (by about an order of magnitude compared to fp64 with excesses exceeding two orders of magnitude). As a consequence, this implementation leads to a systematic drift in the result space and has difficulty resolving close encounters. Posits and fp64 have difficulty when integrating a dynamical system in a moving reference frame; testing Galileo invariancy. In their current implementation, Posits do not seem to be the ideal alternative for fp64 when integrating chaotic or stiff ordinary differential equations, such as Newton's equations of motion.
item.dc:creator: Simon Portegies Zwart (Leiden Observatory)

item.title: From elementary processes to chaos: a discrete-time two-stage contagion model and its continuous limit
item.description: arXiv:2611.08353v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Two-stage contagion, in which adoption requires two contacts with adopters, combined with population turnover produces bistability and relaxation oscillations, but no chaos, in Katriel's differential equations. From the elementary reactions, without reference to the differential equations, we derive a discrete-time model in which the population is updated in rounds of length $\tau$, as in elections, meetings or turns of a game: each individual makes at most one transition per round, events compete as exponential risks, and adoptions take effect from the next round. The model is a Markov chain whose large-population limit is a map $F_\tau$; Katriel's equations are recovered as $\tau\to0$. Taking the probability $p$ of adoption after a single contact as bifurcation parameter, with rates and round length fixed, $F_\tau$ goes from extinction through a window of chaos to a stable equilibrium; for $\beta/\gamma=46$, $\mu/\gamma=0.002$, $\gamma\tau=5.5$ the computed window is $0.023\le p\le0.056$, bounded by the invasion threshold and by a boundary crisis beyond a subcritical Neimark--Sacker point. One-stage contagion ($p=1$), $p=0$ and permanent adoption showed no chaos in our scans. In all tests the chaotic attractor was unique up to coexistence with simpler attractors, with one positive Lyapunov exponent. In the same window Katriel's equations have a periodic relaxation cycle with troughs of $10^{-44}$--$10^{-164}$: the round structure does not create the oscillation but turns it into chaos and shrinks the oscillatory range in $p$ from $(0.022,0.41)$ to $(0.022,0.056)$. The chaos is thus not an artefact of discretising a stable state, but a property of two-stage contagion with synchronous updating.
item.dc:creator: Francisco J. Mu\~noz, Juan Carlos Nu\~no, Luca Meacci
